newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon issues new IDs for first time since war.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon issues new IDs for first time since war.

text.p: Lebanon's ministry of interior began issuing new identification cards for the first time since the start of the 1975-90 civil war.

President Elias Hrawi was issued on Monday the first of the supposedly fraud-proof magnetic cards which do not openly display the holder's religion -- a gesture that the war, which was often fought along sectarian lines, is fading into memory.

It is the first time in Lebanon's history that ID cards do not openly display the holder's faith as the reference to the bearer's religion is entered in a bar strip which can be read only by special government decoders.

Lebanese have 16 months to apply for the new cards before the minisry of interior cancels the old cards. The government stopped issuing identity cards at the start of the war because of widespread counterfeiting and replaced them with civil registration papers.
